script.title: Bihar's AI Leap: Training Teachers and Students for the Future
script.script:
In the heart of eastern India, a quiet revolution is taking shape. The Bihar Education Department has signed a landmark agreement with eleven technology giants, including Google, to bring Artificial Intelligence and IT training to its teachers. This is not just about hardware; it is about empowering the men and women who shape young minds every single day. For years, the conversation around Bihar's education has often focused on challenges. But now, the narrative is shifting. The state is turning a new page, aiming to bridge the digital divide and bring its classrooms into the 21st century.

So, what exactly is this partnership? Reportedly, the Education Department has teamed up with industry leaders like Google Education and other IT firms. The goal is clear: to train teachers in the fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence and Information Technology. But this is not a top-down mandate alone. The department has decided that from the next academic session, computer education will become mandatory for students from class six and above. To make this a reality, the focus is on building the foundation first. Reports suggest that seven hundred model schools will be developed with smart classrooms, with plans to roll this out to other schools in a phased manner.

The training mechanism is reportedly designed for practical impact. A centralized training setup will be operated out of the SCERT campus. Teachers will be trained in different batches, and the training will include hands-on, practical sessions. The headmasters of schools will nominate the teachers for these programs. And importantly, the target is to have this entire infrastructure and training arrangement in place by January of the coming year. Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari has emphasized that the special focus here is on using AI to improve the quality of teaching and learning.

Why does this matter? For the students of Bihar, this means exposure to skills that are increasingly vital in the global economy. For the teachers, it means professional growth and the chance to bring innovative methods into their classrooms. And for the state, it is a step towards transforming Bihar from a talent supplier into a self-reliant tech hub. The Chief Minister has reviewed the 'Bihar AI Policy 2026', aiming to train five hundred thousand youths in AI over the next five years. With these concurrent efforts—training teachers and mandating computer education—Bihar is laying the groundwork for a future where its youth are not just prepared for the jobs of tomorrow, but are equipped to create them.

It is a bold step, rooted in the belief that quality education and technology can go hand-in-hand. The journey has just begun, and the eyes of the nation are watching as Bihar takes this significant stride forward.
